title: Out-of-band swap tests assert the destination id

facts.note: Only test files/test cases are in scope; existing unchanged tests are covered as well as new or edited ones.
Needs a per-test-case content scan (htmx_tester_detector) to see that the case body references `hx-swap-oob` in any form (assertion or not).

values: htmx_tester_detector: oob mention without id-reaching assertion
facts.note: Detector finding: case mentions hx-swap-oob but has no id-reaching assertion.
Non-gating hint only; the rule applies to qualifying test cases regardless of task wording.

fires: A test case asserts the response contains `hx-swap-oob` and has no assertion reaching the destination id.
An existing, unchanged test case only checks that `hx-swap-oob` is present and is scanned by the suite check.
A test case body mentions `hx-swap-oob` anywhere (e.g. in a fixture string, comment or helper argument, not as an assertion) and contains no id-reaching assertion.
doesNotFire: A test case that never mentions `hx-swap-oob`.
A test case mentioning `hx-swap-oob` that also has any id-reaching assertion (`id=` in an expected string, `getElementById`, `querySelector('#…')`, `toHaveAttribute('id'…)`, or another matcher).
Production handler/template code that emits the oob element (covered by the coder-side rule, not this one).

given: A test case whose body mentions `hx-swap-oob`, e.g. asserting an out-of-band swap is present in a response
when: the test case is present in the suite (new, changed or existing)
then: The same test case MUST also assert the destination `id` the out-of-band element will be matched against.
prefer: Assert the destination, not just the mechanism: `expect(html).toContain("hx-swap-oob"); // the server's half only` then `expect(html).toContain('id="cart-count"'); // the half that must match the page`.
Any id-reaching assertion works; no specific matcher is required.
Bind the runtime-artefact assertion back to the declaration it came from: the id the page declares.
avoid: Half assertions: checking `hx-swap-oob` appears and stopping — proves only the server's half, not the destination a template refactor breaks.
An id assertion unrelated to the oob element's destination, just to satisfy the detector.
unless: The test case never mentions `hx-swap-oob` (out of scope).
why: htmx silently drops an oob element whose id matches nothing in the document (no error, no warning, no swap); the id must be in the response AND the document. The coder rule makes the server emit an id; only this rule makes a test prove it is the id the page will match.
evidence: Every test case whose body mentions `hx-swap-oob` contains at least one id-reaching assertion.
htmx_tester_detector reports no findings across the test suite.
Reviewer note: whether the id actually EXISTS in the served document is a runtime fact no static check can see; static compliance only proves the test asserts an id.
verifier_detail: Detector (validator `htmx_tester_detector`): flag a test case whose body mentions `hx-swap-oob` (any mention, not only assertions) but contains no assertion reaching an id.

Id-reaching assertions recognised: an `id=` inside an expected string, a `getElementById` call, a `querySelector('#…')`, or a `toHaveAttribute('id'…)`. Any id-reaching assertion satisfies the rule; no specific matcher is required.
Scope: cases that never mention `hx-swap-oob` are not inspected; all other test cases are, whether or not they changed.
Limitation: existence of the id in the served document is a runtime fact outside the static check.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Bun/htmx realization: the tester half of `coder.htmx.swap-oob-carries-id`; same shape as `tester.convex.interlocking-trace-binds-declared-route` — an assertion on a runtime artefact must bind back to the declaration it came from.

`coder.htmx.swap-oob-carries-id` makes the server EMIT an id; nothing else makes a test prove it is the id the page will actually match. The two rules are one defect seen from source and from suite, and neither alone closes it — which is exactly why the htmx tester surface is a package rather than a stray rule in the Bun one.
Severity 3; disposition strict (fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).

Glossary: destination_id = the `id` htmx matches an out-of-band element against; must be present in the response AND in the document, or the swap does not happen. half_assertion = a test confirming `hx-swap-oob` appears in the response and stopping there; it proves the server's half and nothing about the destination — the half a template refactor breaks.

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: the pack fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
